Subject: Tuesday reading club — new numbers before the review

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, both to give you some encouraging news about the Tuesday reading club and to tell you about something I should have checked with you first.

I understood the concerns in your email of 30 October about pausing the club from January, with attendance low and the hall insurance going up. Since then, though, the numbers have taken a very heartening turn. We had five children most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and fourteen last Tuesday, 3 November. I’m thrilled to see it beginning to take hold, and I wanted to make sure you had those figures before the meeting.

The club has been running since September 2025, on Tuesdays from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library. It has taken time to build, but there is a lovely feeling in the room now. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another child, who wouldn’t open a book in September, asked last week if he could take two home. Those small moments mean a great deal.

We have also had a generous donation from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives us much more choice for the children, particularly as their interests and confidence develop.

I know the increased attendance doesn’t resolve the insurance question, but I hope it gives us grounds to reconsider the pause. It would be a terrible pity to stop just as the club seems to be finding its feet. Would you bring the new figures into the review on the 18th and consider whether there is a way to keep it going?

The other matter is a possible newspaper visit. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market and got carried away telling her about the club. I said, “Come along any Tuesday.” She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple. I know that photographs of the children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. My invitation was not mine to give, and I wanted you to hear about it from me rather than be taken by surprise.

The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it is done properly. I’m happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you have decided whether it should go ahead. If you do approve it, I can collect the consent forms myself, following whatever arrangements you need us to make. There should be no photographs without your approval and the necessary consents in place.

Thank you for considering all of this, Niamh. I’m genuinely delighted by the progress the children are making, and hopeful that we can give the club a chance to build on it.

Warm wishes,

[Your name]
